headline: Dharwad faces child malnutrition challenge: 20% of children affected, with poverty and food insecurity as key drivers
summary: Malnutrition remains a severe challenge in Dharwad district, where 20% of children are malnourished. Contributing factors include poverty, agricultural livelihoods limiting access to nutritious food, and male preference in food distribution within families. 65% of women in the district are themselves malnourished, perpetuating the cycle. Child marriage is also prevalent—Dharwad is among the districts with alarmingly high rates, leading to early pregnancy and increased health risks. Despite health service and sanitation improvements, lack of a holistic approach hampers progress.

Dharwad has alarmingly high rates of child marriage, leading to early pregnancy in girls whose bodies cannot withstand pregnancy rigours

modelFactorWhy.why: The pages do not provide district-specific data on preschool enrollment or early childhood education participation rates for children aged 3-6 in Dharwad.
modelFactorWhy.mechanism: Early schooling supports cognitive development and may improve nutrition access through mid-day meals and health screenings.

modelFactorWhy.factor: Mothers who took iron-folic acid for 180+ days in pregnancy
modelFactorWhy.why: While the pages confirm widespread maternal malnutrition (65% of women) and increased risks in teenage pregnancies studied at SDM Medical College including anaemia, there is no specific data on iron-folic acid supplementation compliance in Dharwad.
modelFactorWhy.mechanism: Adequate iron-folic acid intake during pregnancy prevents maternal anaemia and supports fetal growth, reducing low birth weight and stunting risk.
